title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
statement: You are given a rectangular grid `matrix` in which every cell holds `0` or `1`. Count the square blocks of cells (contiguous rows and columns, side length 1 or more) whose cells are all `1`, and return that count. Squares of every size are counted, and overlapping squares are counted separately.
constraints: Every row of matrix has the same length
notes:
## Intuition

Testing every top-left corner and every side length directly costs far too much on a 300 by 300 grid. Instead, look at each cell as the **bottom-right corner** of squares. If the largest all-ones square ending at a cell has side `k`, then exactly `k` squares end there (sides 1 through `k`), so summing those largest sides over all cells gives the answer.

A square of side `k` can end at a `1` cell only if squares of side `k - 1` end at its upper, left and upper-left neighbours. So the largest side is one more than the smallest of those three values.

## Approach

1. Make `dp` one row and one column larger than `matrix`, filled with `0`, so the first row and column need no special case.
2. Visit cells row by row. `dp[r][c]` describes `matrix[r - 1][c - 1]`.
3. For a `1` cell, read `up`, `left` and `diagonal` from `dp` and set `dp[r][c] = 1 + min(up, left, diagonal)`. A `0` cell keeps `0`.
4. Add `dp[r][c]` to `total`, then return `total`.

## Example 1, step by step

The largest sides ending at each cell come out as:

| row | values | row sum |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 1 1 1 | 3 |
| 1 | 1 1 2 2 | 6 |
| 2 | 0 1 2 3 | 6 |

For the bottom-right cell, `up = 2`, `left = 2`, `diagonal = 2`, so it ends a square of side `3`. Adding all values gives `3 + 6 + 6 = 15`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m·n): each cell is computed once from three neighbours.
- Space: O(m·n) for `dp` (one row would also do, since only the previous row is read).

## Pitfalls

- Add the side length `dp[r][c]`, not just 1: a cell ending a 3-square also ends a 2-square and a 1-square.
- Take the minimum of all three neighbours; checking only `up` and `left` misses a hole on the diagonal.
- Keep the padding offset straight: `dp[r][c]` belongs to `matrix[r - 1][c - 1]`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `cols` | the grid's height and width |
| `dp` | `dp[r][c]` is the side of the largest all-ones square ending at `matrix[r - 1][c - 1]` |
| `total` | squares counted so far |
| `r`, `c` | current position in `dp` (one more than the matrix index) |
| `up`, `left`, `diagonal` | the three neighbours' largest sides |
